summary: Restoration is the main pillar: the DRC targets 7 million ha of afforestation or woodland, 4 million ha of reforestation, 8 million ha under the Bonn Challenge and sustainable land management, one billion trees, and a 6.5% forest-cover increase equal to 15,242,500 ha—about 8.0% of current mapped forest. Conservation combines an existing 13% national-park allocation and a 30%-of-territory protection target by 2030 with 63.5% forest-cover stabilization and 2.2–2.5 Gt CO2e in cumulative forestry emissions reductions. Agriculture plans to double cultivated area from 8 to 16 million ha by 2025, equivalent to about 62% of current mapped agriculture, while reaching 25–75% of holdings through productivity programmes and developing 1 million ha of irrigated land. Cross-cutting measures include 2.5 million ha of community forest concessions by 2025, a 10% urban firewood-share cut by 2025 and 50% by 2031, and a 28% AFAT emissions reduction by 2030.
